claims.claim_verbatim: The parent optimal policy is the reservation rule: compute reservation values z_d solving E[(X_d − z_d)^+] = c_d; open donors in decreasing order of z_d; stop when the best observed value exceeds the reservation value of every unopened donor; take the best observed value.
claims.source_as_cited: Weitzman 1979, Optimal Search for the Best Alternative, Econometrica 47(3), doi:10.2307/1910412

verified_source.title: Optimal Search for the Best Alternative

claims.correction_note: Reservation functional equation, decreasing-z order rule, and stop-when-best-observed-exceeds-every-unopened-reservation-value rule all match the paper as characterized by the publisher and JSTOR full-text snippets. Full text is paywalled; verification used the Econometric Society abstract, a JSTOR body snippet naming Pandora's Rule and the reservation-price definition, and two independent scholarly restatements of z_i via c_i = E[(X_i - z_i)^+] (Olszewski arXiv:1509.09095; Gergatsouli-Tzamos NeurIPS 2023). With Weitzman's discount factor the definition generalizes; the PR's undiscounted form is the standard special case.
claims.evidence_quote: For m = 1, the optimality of Pandora's Rule is easily demonstrated just by directly applying the definition of reservation price.
claims.evidence_location: JSTOR stable/1910412 body snippet (Sec. 2, reservation price); publisher abstract (econometricsociety.org): 'The optimal strategy is an elementary reservation price rule, where the reservation prices are easy to calculate and have an intuitive economic interpretation.'

claims.claim_verbatim: adaptive greedy achieves the parent near-optimality guarantees within the registered constraint class: a near 1-1/e approximation for adaptive value maximization under a cardinality-style budget and a logarithmic competitive ratio for adaptive minimum-cost cover; in the nonadaptive special case with monotone submodular value under a single knapsack budget, greedy with partial enumeration achieves 1-1/e exactly (Sviridenko).

claims.correction_note: Golovin-Krause CONFIRMED (the PR's 'HTTP 404 both fetch attempts' was a wrong URL; live canonical is jair.org/index.php/jair/article/view/10731, DOI 10.1613/jair.3278 printed on the page). Adaptive greedy (1-1/e) under a cardinality budget is verified verbatim. The min-cost-cover guarantee's exact form (Thm 5.8) is c_avg(pi) <= alpha*c_avg(pi*_avg)*(ln(Q/eta)+1) for self-certifying instances and *(ln(Q/(delta*eta))+1) in general, delta = min_phi p(phi) - so 'O(log(1/p_*))-competitive' is a shorthand valid only when Q/eta is constant. Sviridenko WORDING_IMPRECISE: the algorithm enumerates all feasible sets of cardinality ONE OR TWO in phase 1 and ALL 3-element sets U (|U|=3) greedily completed in phase 2 ('For all U subset I such that |U| = 3'), i.e. partial enumeration over TRIPLES (sets of cardinality <= 3), not 'over pairs'. Theorem 1 verbatim: 'The worst-case performance guarantee of the above greedy algorithm for solving problem (1) is equal to 1 - e^-1'; O(n^5) function evaluations.
claims.evidence_quote: we see that the greedy policy which selects k items adaptively obtains at least (1-1/e)
claims.evidence_location: GK 2011 Sec. 5 (stochastic maximization, via Theorem 5.2), JAIR 42 p.~455 in PDF; also Thm 5.8 statement for min-cost cover; Sviridenko 2004 Theorem 1 and Sec. 2 algorithm, ORL 32(1):41-43.

claims.correction_note: Correct title is 'Non-stochastic Best Arm Identification and HYPERPARAMETER Optimization' (not 'Hyperband Applications'; Hyperband/Li et al. is a different paper and is not cited by the PR). Venue is AISTATS 2016 (JMLR W&CP v51), not ICML. The proven guarantee (Thm 1) is sufficiency: any budget B > z_SH returns the best arm (doubling trick: 2*z_SH); Thms 2-4 compare SH to the UNIFORM ALLOCATION baseline - 'provably outperforms the uniform allocation baseline in favorable conditions, and performs comparably (up to log factors) otherwise' - NOT 'within logarithmic factors of the non-stochastic lower bound': a matching lower bound is explicitly a conjecture ('We conjecture that a matching lower bound to Theorem 1 can be derived by considering a stochastic adversary'). The '(K/Δ^2) log K' form is the stochastic-setting complexity (Karnin-Koren-Somekh, ref [15], the acknowledged SH origin: 'the Successive Halving algorithm of [15]'); the non-stochastic bound is stated via envelope functions z_SH, and [15] is missing from the PR's parent list.
claims.evidence_quote: If the Successive Halving algorithm is run with any budget B > zSH then the best arm is guaranteed to be returned.
claims.evidence_location: PMLR v51 jamieson16.pdf, Theorem 1 (p. 243); baseline comparison in abstract and Thms 2-4; lower-bound status in Sec. 6 Future directions; SH origin credit to [15] Karnin-Koren-Somekh (ICML 2013) in Sec. 2.1 and Fig. 3 caption.

Under 1-3, nuclear-norm minimization recovers R exactly with high probability.

claims.correction_note: Publisher abstract (Springer FoCM 9(6):717-772) confirms the exponent exactly: 'm >= C n^{1.2} r log n' with n^{1.2} = n^{6/5}, uniform at random sampling, minimum-nuclear-norm program, perfect recovery with very high probability - matching the PR's assumptions. Two nuances, not defects in the PR: the abstract quantifies over 'most n-by-n matrices of rank r' (random-orthogonal model; incoherence enters via the body theorems for arbitrary matrices) and assumes 'the rank is not too large' - replacing the 1.2 exponent with 1.25 gives the all-ranks result. The PR's closing note 'improved by later work toward near-linear sampling' refers to follow-ups outside the cited 2009 paper and was not verified here.
claims.evidence_quote: if the number m of sampled entries obeys m >= C n^{1.2} r log n ... most n-by-n matrices of rank r can be perfectly recovered by solving a simple convex optimization program
claims.evidence_location: Publisher abstract, FoCM 9(6):717-772, DOI 10.1007/s10208-009-9045-5 (identical text on arXiv:0805.4471 v1 abstract).

claims.correction_note: Russell-Wefald CONFIRMED: general utility-of-computation formula, computations treated as actions selected by utility, resource-bounded rationality framing (abstract + Sec. 3 verbatim from the scanned original). Hay et al. content WRONG_ATTRIBUTION on two points: (1) no later title 'Bounded rational metareasonation' exists - the canonical title IS 'Selecting Computations: Theory and Applications' (UAI 2012); the parenthetical is garbled and should be deleted (the registry's 'selecting computations under limited resources' likewise misstates it). (2) 'their analysis includes Pandora-like settings' is unsupported: the full text contains ZERO Pandora/Weitzman content (no matches for pandora|weitzman in the complete PDF text). What the paper actually proves: metalevel selection as a belief-state MDP; Thm 7 (myopic computes => optimal computes); Thm 9 (myopic stops in a transition-closed subset => optimal stops); Thm 10 (one-armed Bernoulli: optimal policy performs at most lambda(1-lambda)/c - 3 <= 1/4c - 3 computations); counterexamples that optimal policies may compute forever (Ex. 3) and optimal index policies (Gittins) may not exist (Ex. 4); the myopic policy 'has a tendency to stop too early'. Myopic optimality is structure-specific (transition-closed subsets), not Pandora-type.
claims.evidence_quote: We develop a general formula for the utility of computations, this utility being derived directly from the ability of computations to affect an agent's external actions.
claims.evidence_location: Russell-Wefald 1991 abstract (AIJ 49, CMU IIIF scan). Hay et al. quotes at arXiv:1207.5879: Def. 6 + Thms 7/9/10 (Sec. 2), Ex. 3-4 (Sec. 2-3).
